chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had a wet dream, then when morning came he looked at his garment and did not see anything on it.
He said: “He may perform salat in it.”
I said: Then a man saw in a dream that he had a wet dream, then when he arose he found a small amount of moisture on the tip of his private part.
He said: “Ghusl is not upon him. Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: ‘Ghusl is only from the greater fluid.’”

key_terms.اَلْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath required in cases of janabah
key_terms.اَلْمَاءِ اَلْأَكْبَرِ: the major fluid that necessitates ghusl
key_terms.اِحْتَلَمَ: experienced a wet dream during sleep
key_terms.بَلَلًا: a small moisture or wetness found on the body
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment or clothing being checked for traces
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: he performs salat, indicating permissibility of prayer in the garment

ai.seo_question: When is ghusl required after a dream about ejaculation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning suspected janabah after sleep. It indicates that if no trace is found on the garment, or only a slight moisture is found without certainty of major discharge, ghusl is not required, and the garment remains fit for salat.
